title: Old Man's War
author: John Scalzi
summary: On his seventy-fifth birthday a widower joins the colonial army. In return for a stint of service, his old body is replaced by a young, powerful one, and he is sent to fight in wars among the stars.
readIf: you like wisecracking military science fiction with a likeable narrator and a clear, quick pace.
skipIf: you want a deep look at the ethics of war, since it is more entertainment than argument.

pairings.reason: A grimmer, more angry classic that asks what a never-ending space war does to soldiers.
The older model for the genre, with a more serious and militaristic look at service.
Another fast, funny and snarky narrator, with a lot of heart and a much smaller scale.
